correctness.rationale: PASS: Substituting z^n gives the specified bounded backward-shift weights. For reduced p/q, w_n=0 exactly at multiples of q, so D^q=0 while D^(q−1)e_(q−1) is nonzero. For irrational alpha the norm of D^k is the supremum of length-k adjacent sine-weight products; density of the rotation changes this to a maximum over phase x. The log potential u(x)=log|2sin πx| has integral 0: integral of its k-step translate sum forces maximum ≥0, while continuous upper truncations u_M=max(u,−M) and *uniform* unique-ergodicity yield limsup max/k ≤ integral u_M→0. Thus r(D)=(2sinπα)^−1. The established unilateral-shift disk spectrum theorem gives the full disk. Solving eigenvector recurrence yields the exact series, with zero always an eigenvalue. Gayfulin–Hauke Theorem 1 supplies P_N bounded away from zero for eventual CF a_j≤3; the extremely lacunary Liouville expansion forces P_(q_m)^(1/q_m)→0, so coefficients of any nonzero-eigenvalue candidate fail to decay. Independence check reconstructed the norm formulas and sampled Sudler geometric means; general claims follow from the analytic proof and explicitly identified primary theorem.

final_claim: The symmetric recurrence derivative D_alpha on classical H²(D) is a bounded backward weighted shift w_n=sin(nπalpha)/sin(πα). Its spectrum is {0} when alpha=p/q rational (nilpotent index q), and the full disk radius (2sinπα)^(-1) when alpha irrational. Its exact nonzero point-spectrum is governed by Σ_N (|lambda|/R)^(2N)/P_N(alpha)^2<∞; eventually continued-fraction partial quotients ≤3 imply all interior points are eigenvalues, while an explicit Liouville alpha has none.
